p.i: Eius erant hæ sententiæ: Talis esto filius, quales cognatos habere cupis, Malum mortem, bonum magis uitium formidat. Quæsita legendo, serua: quæ nescis, legendo disce. Acquè [?] turpe est carere amicis, atq; eos sæpe mutare. Regi turpius est uinci beneficijs, quàm armis.

main_text.head: 139. CLEMENS sextus.
main_text.p: Clemens sextus, patria Lemouicensis, professio-ne Benedictinus, Petrus Rogerius antea nuncupatus, & abbas Fiscanensis ex Rhotomagensi archi-episcopo, Avenione pontifex Benedicto surrogatus fuit. Hic sua factione supra modum Roma-num turbavit imperium. Episcopos enim omnes, & principes, cum Imperatore Ludovico Bavaro sentientes (Nauclero teste) excommunicavit, in contumeliam eius creabat Vicecomites, Imperij vicarios: & ille uicissim Ludovicus in ecclesia ditione, Imperij uicarios posuit. Hieronymus Marius in Eusebio captiuo, Clementis uiolentiam sic describit: Clemens sextus, inquit, homo mulierum, honoris ac potentiæ cupidissimus, diabolico furore percitus, literas scriptas foribus templorum affixit, quibus imperatori grauissimarum pœnarum supplicium comminabatur, nisi infra triduum suis satisfaceret cupiditatibus, & ab occupatione iu-rium [?]

page.notes: Lines at the top are italic and partly faded; "Acquè" (first word of the third sentence) is doubtful and may be "Atque". The final word "rium" at the bottom right is faint; the reading "iurium" is inferred from the hyphenated line end. "fentientes" in the scan is read as "sentientes". The long s has been normalised to s throughout, and u/v and i/j are normalised per the rules, so "Bauaro", "Auenione" and "turbauit" appear as "Bavaro", "Avenione" and "turbavit". No marginal notes, catchword or signature are printed on this page.
